text_blocks.snippet: Alzheimer's disease (AD) therapeutics can be broadly categorized into two main areas: symptomatic treatments and disease-modifying therapies (DMTs). Symptomatic treatments, like cholinesterase inhibitors (e.g., donepezil, galantamine, rivastigmine), aim to manage cognitive and behavioral symptoms of AD. Disease-modifying therapies, on the other hand, target the underlying biological processes of AD, such as amyloid plaques, tau tangles, neuroinflammation, and synaptic dysfunction.
